prompt: Nobody in the office knows how the network works until it breaks and someone has to trace every cable.
tells: until it breaks and someone has to trace every cable
why: The network is treated as one thing that simply works, and its parts only come into view when it fails. That's something that just works.
trap: The hidden part here is the system's workings, not a person's unseen effort.

prompt: Payroll is just press the button on Friday; only when it failed did anyone learn it used three old systems.
why: People knew only the input and output, not the parts inside, until it broke. Smoothly working things hide their insides.
trap: The three old systems may be locked in, but the point is that nobody saw them while it worked.

prompt: Loan officers trust the credit score without knowing how it is calculated.
tells: without knowing how it is calculated
why: The score is treated as a single trusted output with its workings out of view. That's something that just works, until someone questions it.
trap: People aren't changing behaviour to hit the score; they just trust it without looking inside.

prompt: Printing from any laptop felt like magic until the update broke it and IT had to untangle drivers, servers and settings.
tells: felt like magic until the update broke it
why: When it worked, all its parts were invisible. Breaking opened it up again. That's something that just works.
trap: The breakage blocks printing, but the clue is that its insides were hidden while it worked.

prompt: Writers rely on spellcheck all day and never think about how it decides what is a word.
tells: never think about how it decides
why: A tool used so smoothly its workings disappear from view is something that just works.
trap: It's not hidden human labour; it's the tool's own workings people stop seeing.

prompt: Clean water comes from the tap, and few people think about the pipes and plants behind it until there's a boil-water notice.
why: A huge system shrinks to one tap that just works, and only a failure reminds people what's inside. That's something that just works.
trap: Workers do maintain it, but the clue is the whole system vanishing behind a tap.
